The paper's whole subject is light collection in large NaI(Tl), yet it never states what reflector sits between the crystal and its copper encapsulation, nor the optical coupling compound -- while separately noting results 'hinting at problems with the optical coupling'. Surface preparation is described only for the older PIII module ('polished and cleaned'), not for the AS units this number comes from. The paper also notes DAMA/LIBRA phase 1 reports 5.5-7.5 p.e./keV total for the same material, a factor of two below this work.

column24: Derived by the authors from the detected photoelectron yield and the manufacturer's PMT quantum efficiency. The abstract calls the QE-corrected quantity 'above 40 photoelectrons/keV'; dividing photoelectrons by a quantum efficiency gives photons, so this appears to be a unit error in the abstract of a peer-reviewed paper -- and it is exactly the photons/photoelectrons conflation this survey is built to count. Recorded here as photons/keV, which is what the quantity is. The same paper's introduction cites 40,000 photons/MeV for NaI(Tl), against 38,000 in Bonesini and 41,000 in Roberts et al.
